messages:
clara_sales: Quick heads-up 1 Spectrum Health wants a concise connectivity playbook for a 3-week Private deploy POC. Their security team asks: PrivateLink vs VPC peering, static egress for partner allowlists, firewall rules (ports + FQDNs), TLS-inspect implications for mobile SDKs, and gating items that could delay kickoff. Can we assemble a one-pager?

mike_neteng: Short answer: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is our default recommendation for POCs. Fewer side effects than peering (no full-route exposure). Two integration patterns: customer creates the interface endpoint in their account (cross-account) or grant us a limited IAM role so we create ENIs in their subnets. Cross-account endpoint is usually lower friction.

ev an_solutions: Static egress options to present: 1) Customer-owned NAT gateway + EIP(s) (fastest, recommended for allowlisting). 2) Redwood-reserved egress IPs (add-on with provisioning lead time ~3-7 business days and a small monthly fee). For a short POC ask customer to provide EIPs.

sophie_sec: TLS inspection note: We do NOT perform TLS MITM by default. If Spectrum requires TLS inspection, advise a customer-managed forward proxy. TLS-MITM can break certificate pinning and some mobile SDKs; any request for in-platform interception requires legal/compliance signoff and will add lead time. Also mention BYOK/KMS options for Private deployments if they need key control.

mike_neteng: Pasteable firewall snippet we can give ops:
```
Allow inbound from Redwood connector (PrivateLink ENI IPs or peered CIDR):
- TCP 443 -> endpoint IPs (required for API)
- TCP 80 -> optional (health checks)
- UDP 123 -> optional (NTP)
- ICMP -> optional (diagnostics)
If using VPC peering: add route table entry for Redwood peering CIDR and tighten SGs to only the service subnets. Peering exposes routing between VPCs so only use if customer accepts that scope.
```

ev an_solutions: FQDNs if they insist: api.redwood-inference.net, metrics.redwood-inference.net. Note: FQDN allowlists are less deterministic for interface endpoints; prefer IP allowlist.

sophie_sec: DDoS and rate-limit responsibilities: customer should rely on their cloud provider (e.g., AWS Shield/Azure DDoS). Redwood offers per-route rate-limits and application throttles but does not provide managed scrubbing. We'll include this explicitly in the questionnaire response.

infra-bot: Provision log: test connector created (connector-319) in us-west-2 at 2026-06-02T10:11:09Z.

clara_sales: Blockers checklist to share with Spectrum before kickoff:
- network diagram (subnet CIDRs, NAT ownership, route tables)
- decision on who owns static egress IPs (customer vs Redwood)
- security contact and answers on TLS inspection and cert policies
- IAM approvals for cross-account endpoint or ENI creation if needed
- allowlist entries (their EIPs or our published EIPs)

ev an_solutions: Action items: I'll draft the one-page connectivity playbook + diagram and include an allowlist template. @mike_neteng will add the exact CIDR/EIP ranges we publish.

mike_neteng: I'll provide the allowlist email + example CIDRs by tomorrow EOD.

sophie_sec: I'll prepare the TLS-inspect blurb and compliance caveat for inclusion.

clara_sales: Thanks all 1 will send to the customer once we have the pack. Flagging that if they require Redwood-managed egress + TLS MITM, expect a 2-4 week delay for compliance review. Closing for now :white_check_mark:
